info.title: QAuth Auth Server API
info.description: OAuth 2.1 / OIDC 1.0 authorization server for MCP servers and AI agents: authorization_code + PKCE and client_credentials grants, RFC 8693 on-behalf-of agent delegation, and environment-aware authorization policy. Wallet federation (OID4VP) transport ships behind a default-off flag.

bearerAuth.description: Access token obtained from login, refresh, or OAuth token endpoint.

type.description: The problem type: `https://docs.qauth.dev/reference/problem-types/#` followed by the type's slug.

reasons.description: For `weak_password`: why the new password was refused, in the order checked. A later release may add reasons.

max_age.description: For `insufficient_user_authentication`: the `max_age` of the challenge (RFC 9470 §3), in seconds. Send the person to the authorization endpoint with it, then repeat the call.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Branch on `code`, never on `title` or `detail`. `trace_id` is the id the server logged the request under. `errors` lists each field the request got wrong. `reasons` lists why a new password was refused (`weak_password`). `max_age` says how fresh the next sign-in must be (`insufficient_user_authentication`).

OAuthError.description: An OAuth error (RFC 6749 §5.2). Branch on `error`, never on `error_description`.

get.description: Apple associated domains file: the apps that share the passkeys and passwords of the realm host (`webcredentials`). Served only while the passkey RP ID is the realm host.
Digital Asset Links statement list: the Android apps that share the sign-in credentials of the realm host (`get_login_creds`). Served only while the passkey RP ID is the realm host.
Liveness: answers 200 while the process serves, with the service roles it runs. It checks no dependency; `GET /ready` does. Answers on any host and carries no realm data.

200.description: The process answers. Its dependencies are what `GET /ready` checks.

roles.description: The service roles this process runs (`SERVICE_ROLES`).

schema.description: The process answers. Its dependencies are what `GET /ready` checks.

get.description: Read the current step: the step, the alternatives and their params, a CSRF value for one answer and the realm's brand. The interaction id alone is enough; no personal data. The Interaction API v1-rc.0 (ADR-019 Decision 6); its contract, with every step’s schema, is the document at /interaction/v1-rc.0/openapi.json.

Read the personal data of the current step. Needs the flow cookie; refused from another origin. The Interaction API v1-rc.0 (ADR-019 Decision 6); its contract, with every step’s schema, is the document at /interaction/v1-rc.0/openapi.json.

post.description: Answer the current step with the CSRF value of the step read, as JSON or as a plain HTML form post. Needs the realm origin and the flow cookie. A form post gets 303 to the ceremony page or to the final redirect. The Interaction API v1-rc.0 (ADR-019 Decision 6); its contract, with every step’s schema, is the document at /interaction/v1-rc.0/openapi.json.

Cancel the interaction with the CSRF value of the step read: the client gets access_denied. Needs the realm origin and the flow cookie. The Interaction API v1-rc.0 (ADR-019 Decision 6); its contract, with every step’s schema, is the document at /interaction/v1-rc.0/openapi.json.

get.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document of the Interaction API v1-rc.0, with one JSON Schema per step (ADR-019 Decision 6). The same document the docs site publishes. Unauthenticated, cacheable.

Readiness: runs the checks this process needs for its service roles (the database, Redis, the KEK, the event outbox) and answers 200 when every one passes. When one fails it answers 503 with a `service_unavailable` problem document whose extension members `roles` and `checks` carry the roles and the result of each check, as the 200 answer does. Answers on any host and carries no realm data.

200.description: The readiness checks of this process and their results.

roles.description: The service roles this process runs (`SERVICE_ROLES`).

reason.description: Why a failed check failed: the dependency refused or errored, or did not answer in time.

additionalProperties.description: The result of one readiness check.

checks.description: Each check the roles registered, by name: `database` on every process, `redis` on `web`, `api` and `admin`, `kek` on `signer`, `outbox` on `delivery`.

schema.description: The readiness checks of this process and their results.

get.description: Root API endpoint. Returns a simple greeting to verify the auth server is running.
OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414). Unauthenticated, cacheable.
OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 document. Superset of RFC 8414 AS metadata with OIDC-specific fields. Unauthenticated, cacheable.

JSON Web Key Set (RFC 7517) of the realm the request host names: its published token signing keys (EdDSA, RS256 and, with hybrid signing, ML-DSA-65), each under its own `kid`. Used by clients and resource servers to verify JWT signatures.

Shared Signals Framework transmitter metadata (SSF 1.0 §7): the stream management endpoints, push delivery, and the transmitter’s own JWKS (`/ssf/jwks.json`), which verifies the realm’s Security Event Tokens. 404 for a realm that does not run the transmitter.
List the active OAuth consents of the token's user, one page at a time, by when each was first given, newest first. A new grant to the same client keeps its consent where it is in the list.

delete.description: Revoke one of the token's user's OAuth consents, with every refresh token and unredeemed authorization code issued under it. A consent of another user is 404, as one that does not exist.

get.description: List the upstream accounts linked to the token's user, newest first: the provider and when it was linked, never the identity's subject at the provider.

delete.description: Unlink one of the token's user's upstream accounts: the account no longer signs in through its provider. Needs a fresh sign-in with the account's strongest factor and refuses an act-chain token. The account's last way to sign in is 409 last_credential; one of another user is 404, as one that does not exist.

get.description: Read the token's user's sign-in methods at a glance: whether a password is set and when it was last set, how many passkeys, whether an authenticator app (TOTP) is on, how many recovery codes are left, how many upstream accounts and wallets are linked, whether there is a contact address, and the factor a fresh authentication must hold.

post.description: Change the token's user's password, with the current one. Needs a fresh sign-in with the account's strongest factor and refuses an act-chain token. A wrong current password is 400 invalid_current_password and counts on the account's failure ladder; a new password the realm's password policy or breach list refuses is 422 weak_password with its reasons. Afterwards the account's other browser sessions and its refresh-token families end, the session the token names stays, and the owner is told. An account without a password is 404.

currentPassword.description: The password the account has now.

newPassword.description: The new password. The realm’s password policy and breach list apply.

get.description: List the passkeys bound to the token's user, newest first: each one's name, whether it syncs to other devices, when it was added and when it last signed in. Adding one is no operation here: it runs in the ceremony app on the realm host, through an authorization request with `qauth_action=setup_passkey`.
Read one of the token's user's passkeys, with the `ETag` a rename names. A passkey of another user is 404, as one that does not exist.

patch.description: Rename one of the token's user's passkeys with a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) of its `nickname`. `If-Match` must name the passkey's current `ETag`: 428 without it, 412 when the passkey changed since. A name is no credential, so it needs no fresh sign-in, but an act-chain token is refused. A passkey of another user is 404.

nickname.description: The new name, as display text.

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the representation this update replaces (RFC 9110 §13.1.1).

delete.description: Remove one of the token's user's passkeys. Needs a fresh sign-in with the account's strongest factor, or one that used a recovery code in place of a lost factor; a passkey still new (bound after a sign-in that proved only the password) is removed after a fresh sign-in with the password, and its removal ends the sessions whose sign-in bound or proved it, their codes and refresh tokens, the account's recovery codes and every sign-in in progress. Refuses an act-chain token. The account's last way to sign in is 409 last_credential; the last second factor the realm requires, 409 second_factor_required. The owner gets the "passkey removed" notice. A passkey of another user is 404.

post.description: Start an authenticator-app enrolment for the token's user: a new secret, answered once as text and as an `otpauth://` URI. Nothing is bound until the enrolment is confirmed with a first code within ten minutes; a new enrolment replaces one not yet confirmed. Needs a fresh sign-in with the account's strongest factor, or one that used a recovery code in place of a lost one, and refuses an act-chain token. An account that holds an authenticator app is 409 conflict, unless the sign-in used a recovery code in place of a lost one: that enrolment replaces the app once confirmed. An unclaimed account, and one with no address the app could show, are 409 conflict too.

secret.description: The shared secret, base32 without padding: 160 bits. Shown once.

otpauthUri.description: The same secret as an `otpauth://totp/` URI. Shown once.

expiresAt.description: When the enrolment lapses unless confirmed.

emailCode.description: Whether confirming also needs a mailed code. Always `not_required`: the account, not a mailbox, decides (ADR-017 Decision 8).

post.description: Bind the started enrolment's secret with a first valid code. A wrong code is 400 invalid_code and binds nothing; the enrolment waits for another. The account's first second factor also issues its first set of recovery codes, answered once. The "authenticator app added" notice goes out. Without a started enrolment, or after it lapsed, the answer is 404. Needs a fresh sign-in as the start does, and refuses an act-chain token.

code.description: The first code the authenticator app shows.

emailCode.description: A mailed code. No enrolment asks for one; it is ignored.

enabledAt.description: When the authenticator app was bound.

codes.description: The ten codes. Shown once: the server keeps only their hashes.

delete.description: Remove the token's user's authenticator app. Needs a fresh sign-in with the account's strongest factor, or one that used a recovery code in place of a lost app, the first half of a rebind; an app still new (bound after a sign-in that proved only the password) is removed after a fresh sign-in with the password, and its removal ends the sessions whose sign-in bound or proved it. Refuses an act-chain token. The last second factor the realm requires is 409 second_factor_required. The owner gets the "authenticator app removed" notice. An account without one is 404.

get.description: How many of the token's user's recovery codes are left, and when the set was issued. Never the codes.

remaining.description: How many unused codes are left.

issuedAt.description: When the current set was issued; `null` without one.

post.description: Issue a new set of ten recovery codes for the token's user, answered once; every code of the old set stops working. Needs a fresh sign-in with the account's strongest factor and refuses an act-chain token. An account without a second factor or a passkey is 409 conflict. The "recovery codes regenerated" notice goes out.

codes.description: The ten codes. Shown once: the server keeps only their hashes.

get.description: List the token's user's live browser sessions, most recently used first: each one's device label, when it started and when it was last used, and `current` on the one the token came through (its `sid`). Never the session's address or cookie.

id.description: The session’s id: its record’s, never the cookie value.

current.description: Whether the token in this request was issued through this session (its `sid`).

label.description: A label from the user agent, such as `Firefox on Linux`.

device.description: The device the session came from.

delete.description: End one of the token's user's sessions: its cookie stops working, its refresh-token families end, and every app it signed in to with a back-channel logout URI is sent a logout token. Needs no fresh sign-in and takes an act-chain token: ending a session only takes access away. A session of another user, or one that has ended, is 404.

post.description: Sign out everywhere: every session of the token's user ends, each app a session signed in to with a back-channel logout URI is sent a logout token, and every unredeemed code and refresh-token family of the user is revoked. The session the token came through stays only when `keepCurrent` is true and the token names it in `sid`, which a refreshed token does not. Needs no fresh sign-in and takes an act-chain token.

keepCurrent.description: Keep the session this request’s token was issued through. Default: end it too.

post.description: Start linking a wallet credential to the signed-in account. Requires a valid session cookie and an `X-CSRF-Token` header matching the per-session token returned by `GET /consents`. Issues an OID4VP 1.0 presentation request in LINKING mode: the validated response is bound to the caller's authenticated users.id and is never used to resolve or create an account (ADR-009 §5). Linking is same-device only (ADR-013, amended 2026-11-07): the wallet must be on the device the browser runs on, the link completes on the browser's return leg at `GET /ui/wallet-login/return`, and the poll answers `pending` until then (OID4VP 1.0 §14.2, HAIP 1.0 §5.1). The optional `device` field accepts only `this`, which is also what an absent field or body means; `other` (cross-device) is refused with `400` `validation_error`. Issues #238, #405.

get.description: Poll a wallet-linking flow. A link is same-device only (ADR-013, amended 2026-11-07): it completes on the return leg, writing a second user_credentials row (provider_type=wallet) under the same users.id, and this poll answers `pending` until then, then `linked` once (#405). A cross-device flow started before that change is answered `rejected`. Issue #238.

post.description: Authenticate with email and password. Returns access token, refresh token, and expiration. Requires valid credentials.

Log out the current user. Ends the user's hosted browser sessions, revokes all refresh tokens and unredeemed authorization codes for the user, and the access token presented. Accepts expired access tokens.

get.description: Landing page of a mailed pass link (the send-ceiling and password-disabled notices). Starts an interaction that holds the pass and redirects (303) to its ceremony page; opening it does not spend the pass. A malformed, unknown, used or expired pass gets an HTML page and no interaction.

post.description: Register a password account. Answers every address with the same 202 and message, whether it was free or already registered; the next step arrives by email (a verification link for a new account, a notice for an existing one). The password must meet the realm's password policy: at least `password.minLength` characters (15 by default) after NFC normalisation, at most 256 UTF-16 code units, not a common word or password or the address, service or realm name as a whole, and a zxcvbn score of at least `password.minScore`. A password over 256 UTF-16 code units is refused by the request schema with a 400 `validation_error`, before the policy runs. A refusal by the policy is a 422 `weak_password` whose `reasons` say why (`too_short`, `blocklisted`, `too_weak`). While the realm's `accounts.allowSignUp` is off (the default), every request is refused with a 403 `forbidden`, before the password or the address is checked.
Request a new verification email. Rate limited per IP and per email. Always returns success to prevent email enumeration.

get.description: Landing page of the emailed verification link. Renders a form that asks for the account password; opening it verifies nothing. The form posts to POST /ui/verify.

post.description: Verify email address using the token sent via email, in the request body. Single-use; marks token as used. POST so no link fetch or prefetch can verify an address on its own.

get.description: List the OAuth clients owned by the authenticated developer. Scoped by oauth_clients.developer_id. Requires a developer Bearer access token. Never returns the client secret. (Phase 2.2, issue #85.)

post.description: Create an OAuth client owned by the authenticated developer. The server generates the client_id and (for confidential clients) a client_secret; the plaintext secret is returned in THIS response only and never again. Requires a developer Bearer access token. (Phase 2.2, issue #86.)

get.description: Get one of the authenticated developer's OAuth clients by id. Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer (no existence enumeration). Never returns the client secret. (Phase 2.2, issue #87.)

patch.description: Update mutable fields of one of the developer's OAuth clients (name, description, redirectUris, scopes, grantTypes, responseTypes, tokenEndpointAuthMethod, enabled). client_id and client_secret are immutable here. enabled is the owner's switch and may be set either way; it does not lift an operator's suspension (the read-only suspended field), which only the operator can. Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer. (Phase 2.2, issue #88.)

delete.description: Delete one of the developer's OAuth clients. Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer. After deletion the client can no longer authenticate. (Phase 2.2, issue #89.)

post.description: Issue a new client_secret for one of the developer's OAuth clients. The previous secret is invalidated immediately and the new plaintext secret is returned in THIS response only. Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer; 400 for a public client that has no secret. (Phase 2.2, issue #90.)

Mint a static developer API key for one of the developer's OAuth clients. ENVIRONMENT-GATED (ADR-008 §6): permitted only while the client resolves to a development environment; a staging/production (or unset-environment) client is refused with 403 and must use the OAuth client_credentials grant. The plaintext key is returned in THIS response only and never again. Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer. (Issue #97.)

get.description: List the static API keys for one of the developer's OAuth clients. Returns masked fields only (prefix + last4) — never the key or its hash. Includes revoked keys (with revokedAt set). Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer. (Issue #97.)

delete.description: Revoke one static API key for one of the developer's OAuth clients. Idempotent soft-delete: the row is retained with revokedAt set, and a revoked key never authenticates again. Returns 404 if the client or key does not exist or is owned by another developer. (Issue #97.)

get.description: List the active OAuth consents for the currently signed-in user. Drives the developer portal revocation screen (issue #150). The response also carries a per-session CSRF token that the caller MUST echo back as the `X-CSRF-Token` header on `DELETE /consents/:id`.

delete.description: Revoke an OAuth consent row owned by the currently signed-in user. Requires a valid `X-CSRF-Token` header whose value matches the session CSRF token returned by `GET /consents`.

get.description: List the active OAuth consents belonging to the authenticated user. Requires a developer Bearer access token. Drives the developer portal revocation screen (issue #366).

delete.description: Revoke one of the authenticated user's OAuth consents. Returns 404 if the consent does not exist or belongs to another user, so the API never reveals that another user's consent id exists. Requires a developer Bearer access token.

get.description: List the OAuth clients the token's developer owns, newest first, one page at a time. A client registered anonymously (dynamic registration, a Client ID Metadata Document) has no owner and is never listed (ADR-012).

post.description: Create an OAuth client owned by the token's developer. The server generates `client_id` and, for a confidential client, `client_secret`, which this answer carries once and never again. The checks of dynamic registration apply: the realm's scope allowlist, the redirect URI rules and the per-developer client limit.

get.description: Read one of the token's developer's OAuth clients, with its `ETag`. A client that does not exist or that another developer owns is 404 (ADR-012). Never returns the client secret.

patch.description: Change one of the token's developer's OAuth clients with a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396). `If-Match` must name the client's current `ETag`: 428 without it, 412 when the client changed since. A member set to `null` takes the value a create gives it when it is left out; `client_name` has none, so `null` there is 422. `enabled` is the owner's switch and does not lift an operator's suspension. A client of another developer is 404.

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the representation this update replaces (RFC 9110 §13.1.1).

delete.description: Delete one of the token's developer's OAuth clients. It can no longer authenticate. A client of another developer is 404.

post.description: Issue a new `client_secret` for one of the token's developer's confidential clients. The previous secret stops working at once; this answer carries the new one once. A public client has no secret (400). A client of another developer is 404.

get.description: List the static API keys of one of the token's developer's clients, newest first, one page at a time: masked fields only, revoked keys included. A client of another developer is 404.

post.description: Mint a static API key for one of the token's developer's clients. Permitted only while the client's effective environment is development (ADR-008 §6); any other is 403 and uses the client_credentials grant. The plaintext `key` is in this answer once and never again. A client of another developer is 404.

delete.description: Revoke one static API key of one of the token's developer's clients, and answer it with `revokedAt` set. Idempotent: the key is kept, revoked, and never authenticates again. A client or key of another developer is 404.

get.description: List the active OAuth consents of the token's user, one page at a time, by when each was first given, newest first. A new grant to the same client keeps its consent where it is in the list.

delete.description: Revoke one of the token's user's OAuth consents, with every refresh token and unredeemed authorization code issued under it. A consent of another user is 404, as one that does not exist.

get.description: OAuth 2.1 authorization endpoint (GET). Issues an authorization code with PKCE and redirects to the client redirect_uri.

parameters.name: dpop_jkt
parameters.description: RFC 9449 §10: the base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the DPoP key to bind the authorization code to. Read only when the server has DPoP on.

parameters.name: login_hint
parameters.description: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §3.1.2.1: a hint at the identifier the person signs in with, at most 254 bytes in UTF-8. Where the sign-in runs as an interaction (INTERACTION_UI_ENABLED), it pre-fills the identifier step; the person may answer it with another identifier. The sign-in page ignores it.

parameters.name: qauth_upstream
parameters.description: QAuth's direct-routing parameter: the type of one of the realm's upstream identity providers (`oidc_<alias>`), hidden ones included. When the request needs a sign-in, the sign-in starts at that provider instead of the first sign-in step. A value that names no provider the realm has on is ignored, as it is when no sign-in is needed.

parameters.name: qauth_link
parameters.description: QAuth's link parameter (#670): the type of one of the realm's upstream identity providers (`oidc_<alias>`), hidden ones included, whose account the person links to theirs. The request starts at that provider, then asks for a fresh sign-in to the existing account with its own factors, whatever session the browser has; the identity joins the account that sign-in proved. Honoured only for an operator-flagged first-party client while the interaction UI is on; any other value, or any other client's, is ignored.

parameters.name: qauth_action
parameters.description: QAuth's set-up parameter (#1108): a change to the account's sign-in methods that runs on the realm origin. `setup_passkey` adds a passkey: a fresh sign-in, whatever session the browser has, then the passkey enrolment, then the code at the redirect URI. The person may decline the enrolment; the code comes back either way, and the account API's passkey list tells what was bound. Only a client whose `audience` lists `urn:qauth:aud:account:v1-rc.0` may ask for it (else `unauthorized_client`), never with `prompt=create` or `qauth_link`, and only while the interaction UI and passkey sign-in are on (else `invalid_request`).

post.description: OAuth 2.1 authorization endpoint (POST). Identical to GET; parameters are form-encoded in the request body (OIDC Core §3.1.2.1).

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 9449 §10: the base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the DPoP key to bind the authorization code to. Read only when the server has DPoP on.

login_hint.description: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §3.1.2.1: a hint at the identifier the person signs in with, at most 254 bytes in UTF-8. Where the sign-in runs as an interaction (INTERACTION_UI_ENABLED), it pre-fills the identifier step; the person may answer it with another identifier. The sign-in page ignores it.

qauth_upstream.description: QAuth's direct-routing parameter: the type of one of the realm's upstream identity providers (`oidc_<alias>`), hidden ones included. When the request needs a sign-in, the sign-in starts at that provider instead of the first sign-in step. A value that names no provider the realm has on is ignored, as it is when no sign-in is needed.

qauth_link.description: QAuth's link parameter (#670): the type of one of the realm's upstream identity providers (`oidc_<alias>`), hidden ones included, whose account the person links to theirs. The request starts at that provider, then asks for a fresh sign-in to the existing account with its own factors, whatever session the browser has; the identity joins the account that sign-in proved. Honoured only for an operator-flagged first-party client while the interaction UI is on; any other value, or any other client's, is ignored.

qauth_action.description: QAuth's set-up parameter (#1108): a change to the account's sign-in methods that runs on the realm origin. `setup_passkey` adds a passkey: a fresh sign-in, whatever session the browser has, then the passkey enrolment, then the code at the redirect URI. The person may decline the enrolment; the code comes back either way, and the account API's passkey list tells what was bound. Only a client whose `audience` lists `urn:qauth:aud:account:v1-rc.0` may ask for it (else `unauthorized_client`), never with `prompt=create` or `qauth_link`, and only while the interaction UI and passkey sign-in are on (else `invalid_request`).

get.description: OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 end-session endpoint. A valid id_token_hint that names the browser session (its account by sub, the session by sid) ends that session at once; otherwise a signed-in browser is asked to confirm, and nothing ends until it answers. Goes back to a registered post_logout_redirect_uri with state, or shows a page; an unregistered one gets an information page and never a redirect. A client the operator did not set up is not redirected to before the browser has seen a QAuth page: the signed-out page links to its return URI. A realm that names its ceremony app’s error page (its ceremonyApp.errorPage policy) gets 303 to that page, on the realm’s own origin, in place of each of these pages. Refresh tokens are not revoked here. Parameters in the query.

parameters.name: id_token_hint
parameters.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2: an ID token this realm issued to the client, expired or not. When it names the browser session (its account by sub, the session by sid), the session ends without a confirmation.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2: the client asking. With an id_token_hint it must be the hint’s audience.

parameters.name: post_logout_redirect_uri
parameters.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2: where the browser goes after the logout. Must be one of the client’s registered post_logout_redirect_uris, matched exactly; otherwise QAuth shows an information page and never redirects.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2: an opaque value added to the post_logout_redirect_uri when the browser goes back.

parameters.name: ui_locales
parameters.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2. Accepted and not read.

parameters.name: logout_hint
parameters.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2. Accepted and not read.

post.description: OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 end-session endpoint. A valid id_token_hint that names the browser session (its account by sub, the session by sid) ends that session at once; otherwise a signed-in browser is asked to confirm, and nothing ends until it answers. Goes back to a registered post_logout_redirect_uri with state, or shows a page; an unregistered one gets an information page and never a redirect. A client the operator did not set up is not redirected to before the browser has seen a QAuth page: the signed-out page links to its return URI. A realm that names its ceremony app’s error page (its ceremonyApp.errorPage policy) gets 303 to that page, on the realm’s own origin, in place of each of these pages. Refresh tokens are not revoked here. Parameters form-encoded in the body. A POST without the session cookie, as a cross-site one, is answered 303 to the same endpoint as a GET with the same parameters, so the browser sends its cookie.

id_token_hint.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2: an ID token this realm issued to the client, expired or not. When it names the browser session (its account by sub, the session by sid), the session ends without a confirmation.

client_id.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2: the client asking. With an id_token_hint it must be the hint’s audience.

post_logout_redirect_uri.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2: where the browser goes after the logout. Must be one of the client’s registered post_logout_redirect_uris, matched exactly; otherwise QAuth shows an information page and never redirects.

state.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2: an opaque value added to the post_logout_redirect_uri when the browser goes back.

ui_locales.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2. Accepted and not read.

logout_hint.description: RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2. Accepted and not read.

get.description: The sign-out status page of RP-initiated logout: whether this browser is still signed in. Takes no parameter. A realm that names its ceremony app’s error page (its ceremonyApp.errorPage policy) gets 303 to that page instead, with code=logout_finished and signed_out.

post.description: RFC 7662 token introspection. Send access token and client credentials in application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. Returns active and claims when token is valid for the client.

OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591). Open-mode — no initial_access_token required. Scope requests are capped to the realm's dynamic_registration_allowed_scopes list, which never holds a scope in QAuth's reserved qauth: namespace. A registration with a developer's access token makes the developer the client's owner; an agent client (is_agent: true) so registered needs an owner whose account is verified, its primary identity proved, and is otherwise refused with 403 access_denied.
RFC 7009 token revocation. Send the token and confidential client credentials in an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. Always returns 200 with an empty body on success.
OAuth 2.1 token endpoint. Supports authorization_code (with PKCE) and client_credentials grants. Client auth via client_secret_post or client_secret_basic.

get.description: OIDC userinfo endpoint (GET). Returns claims for the authenticated user. Requires a Bearer access token whose `aud` contains its own `client_id` or this endpoint's URL, or the developer portal's token: `client_id` the system client and `aud` the developer API's audience, `urn:qauth:aud:developer:v1-rc.0`. A token for another resource server gets 401, as does a token whose subject is not a user (a client_credentials token). With DPoP on, a DPoP-bound token is accepted only under the `DPoP` scheme with a valid proof (RFC 9449 §7), and refused as a Bearer token.

post.description: OIDC userinfo endpoint (POST). Returns claims for the authenticated user. Accepts a Bearer access token in the Authorization header or a form-encoded access_token body parameter (RFC 6750 §2.2). The token's `aud` must contain its own `client_id` or this endpoint's URL, unless it is the developer portal's token: `client_id` the system client and `aud` the developer API's audience, `urn:qauth:aud:developer:v1-rc.0`. A token for another resource server gets 401, as does a token whose subject is not a user (a client_credentials token). With DPoP on, a DPoP-bound token is accepted only under the `DPoP` scheme with a valid proof (RFC 9449 §7), and refused as a Bearer token or a body parameter.

get.description: OID4VP 1.0 / RFC 9101 Request Object Endpoint. Serves the signed Authorization Request a `request_uri` refers to, as application/oauth-authz-req+jwt. TRANSPORT ONLY: the request state is neither read nor consumed here, nothing is written, and an unknown or expired reference is indistinguishable from a malformed one.

post.description: OID4VP 1.0 direct_post Response Endpoint. Accepts a wallet Authorization Response as application/x-www-form-urlencoded: in the clear (vp_token + state, or error + state) under response_mode=direct_post, or as a single `response` parameter carrying a JWE (ECDH-ES P-256, A128GCM/A256GCM) encrypted to the per-request key published in client_metadata under response_mode=direct_post.jwt. TRANSPORT ONLY: the response is correlated against a single-use presentation request and structurally parsed. No signature, credential or issuer validation is performed and no user is authenticated (that is #234/#236). Answers HTTP 200 with a JSON object (OID4VP 1.0 §8.2): `{}` for a cross-device request, or `{ redirect_uri }` for a same-device request — an absolute URI under the issuer carrying a fresh, single-use Response Code (HAIP 1.0 §5.1) that the wallet MUST redirect the user agent to.

200.description: Transport-level acknowledgement (OID4VP 1.0 §8.2): HTTP 200 with a JSON object. Confirms the response was well-formed and correlated with a pending presentation request. For a same-device request the object carries `redirect_uri` — an absolute URI under the issuer with a fresh, single-use Response Code — which the wallet MUST redirect the user agent to (HAIP 1.0 §5.1); for a cross-device request it is empty and the wallet is not required to perform any further steps. It does NOT assert that any credential was verified or that any user was authenticated.

schema.description: Transport-level acknowledgement (OID4VP 1.0 §8.2): HTTP 200 with a JSON object. Confirms the response was well-formed and correlated with a pending presentation request. For a same-device request the object carries `redirect_uri` — an absolute URI under the issuer with a fresh, single-use Response Code — which the wallet MUST redirect the user agent to (HAIP 1.0 §5.1); for a cross-device request it is empty and the wallet is not required to perform any further steps. It does NOT assert that any credential was verified or that any user was authenticated.

get.description: The JSON Web Key Set (RFC 7517) that verifies the realm’s Security Event Tokens: its active and retired `event_signing` keys. The `jwks_uri` of the transmitter metadata. Unauthenticated, cacheable for five minutes. The realm JWKS at `/.well-known/jwks.json` holds no SET key.

post.description: Add a subject to the stream (SSF 1.0 §8.1.3.2). The transmitter’s `default_subjects` is `NONE`: the stream receives events only about the subjects added. A user is named `iss_sub` with the realm’s issuer, a client `uri` or `opaque` by its `client_id`; another subject is kept and matches no event. A user must be related to the receiver: an active consent for its client or a live refresh token its client was issued, or a live refresh token whose audience names the receiver as a resource server (a value of its `audience`, never a `urn:qauth:aud:` value or the realm’s issuer). Any other user, an unknown one included, is refused with 403. A user subject ends once the relation has ended and the events about the user have reached the stream.
Remove a subject from the stream (SSF 1.0 §8.1.3.3). A subject the stream does not have answers 204 as well.

Ask for a verification event on the stream (SSF 1.0 §8.1.4.2). QAuth records the request as an event and pushes the verification Security Event Token to this stream only, with `state` returned as sent. A second request within `min_verification_interval` (10 seconds) answers 429.

get.description: The hosted account page (#844): the browser session’s account, its sign-in methods (password, passkeys, authenticator app, recovery codes, linked upstream accounts) and its live sessions, each with its actions as plain forms. A browser with no session is sent through a sign-in on the hosted pages (`303`) and comes back. Replaced by the account console (#685–#688). `Cache-Control: no-store`.
The hosted "change your password" page (#844): the current password and the new one. Replaced by the account console (#685). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.description: Change the password with the current one (#844; the account API's `account.password.change`). Needs a sign-in from the last five minutes with the account's strongest factor. The new password meets the realm's password policy and breach list, or the page says why not; a wrong current password counts on the failure ladder. The account's other sessions and its refresh tokens end; this session stays.
Confirm it’s you (#844): start a fresh sign-in on the hosted pages, which asks for the account’s strongest factor first, then come back to the account page.
Add a passkey (#844): a fresh sign-in on the hosted pages, then the passkey enrolment step of #651 on the realm origin, then back to the account page. Only while passkeys are on (`WEBAUTHN_ENABLED`).
Rename one of the account's passkeys (#844; `account.passkeys.update`). A name is no credential, so it needs no fresh sign-in; an empty name removes it.

Remove one of the account's passkeys (#844; `account.passkeys.delete`). Needs a sign-in from the last five minutes with the account's strongest factor, or with a recovery code in place of a lost one; a passkey still new (bound after a sign-in that proved only the password, #1064) needs one with the password, and its removal ends the sessions whose sign-in bound or proved it, their codes and their refresh families, the account's recovery codes and every sign-in in progress. The account's last way to sign in, or the last second factor the realm requires, is refused (`409`).
Set up an authenticator app (#844): a fresh sign-in on the hosted pages, then the TOTP set-up step of #653, then back to the account page. An account that has one is refused (`409`).

Turn off the authenticator app (#844; `account.totp.delete`). Needs a sign-in from the last five minutes with the account's strongest factor, or with a recovery code in place of a lost one; an app still new (bound after a sign-in that proved only the password, #1064) needs one with the password, and turning it off ends the sessions whose sign-in bound or proved it, their codes and their refresh families, the account's recovery codes and every sign-in in progress. The last second factor the realm requires is refused (`409`).

Issue a new set of recovery codes (#844; `account.recoveryCodes.regenerate`), shown once on the page this answers: every code of the old set stops working. Needs a sign-in from the last five minutes with the account's strongest factor. An account with no passkey and no authenticator app is refused (`409`). `Cache-Control: no-store`.
Say the new recovery codes are saved (#844). A set a newer one replaced meanwhile is not confirmed, and the page says so.

Sign one of the account's sessions out (#844; `account.sessions.delete`): its cookie stops working, the refresh-token families its sign-in opened end (#1110), and every app it signed in to with a back-channel logout URI is sent a logout token. A session of another account is `404`, untouched.

Sign out everywhere (#844; `account.sessions.endAll`): every session of the account ends, this one too, each app a session signed in to with a back-channel logout URI is sent a logout token, and every refresh token of the account is revoked.

Link an upstream account (#844, #670): the person signs in at the provider, then to this account again, with its own factors or through another provider whose identity the account already holds (#1080), in one interaction on the hosted pages; the identity the provider proved is linked then. Nothing is matched by an email address. Only a provider the realm offers and the account holds no identity of; any other is `404`.

Unlink one of the account's upstream accounts (#844; `account.linkedAccounts.delete`). Needs a sign-in from the last five minutes with the account's strongest factor. The account's last way to sign in is refused (`409`).

get.description: Render the OAuth consent screen. Requires a valid __Host-qauth_session cookie; otherwise redirects to /ui/login.

parameters.name: dpop_jkt
parameters.description: RFC 9449 §10: the base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the DPoP key to bind the authorization code to. Read only when the server has DPoP on.

parameters.name: login_hint
parameters.description: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §3.1.2.1: a hint at the identifier the person signs in with, at most 254 bytes in UTF-8. Where the sign-in runs as an interaction (INTERACTION_UI_ENABLED), it pre-fills the identifier step; the person may answer it with another identifier. The sign-in page ignores it.

parameters.name: qauth_upstream
parameters.description: QAuth's direct-routing parameter: the type of one of the realm's upstream identity providers (`oidc_<alias>`), hidden ones included. When the request needs a sign-in, the sign-in starts at that provider instead of the first sign-in step. A value that names no provider the realm has on is ignored, as it is when no sign-in is needed.

parameters.name: qauth_link
parameters.description: QAuth's link parameter (#670): the type of one of the realm's upstream identity providers (`oidc_<alias>`), hidden ones included, whose account the person links to theirs. The request starts at that provider, then asks for a fresh sign-in to the existing account with its own factors, whatever session the browser has; the identity joins the account that sign-in proved. Honoured only for an operator-flagged first-party client while the interaction UI is on; any other value, or any other client's, is ignored.

parameters.name: qauth_action
parameters.description: QAuth's set-up parameter (#1108): a change to the account's sign-in methods that runs on the realm origin. `setup_passkey` adds a passkey: a fresh sign-in, whatever session the browser has, then the passkey enrolment, then the code at the redirect URI. The person may decline the enrolment; the code comes back either way, and the account API's passkey list tells what was bound. Only a client whose `audience` lists `urn:qauth:aud:account:v1-rc.0` may ask for it (else `unauthorized_client`), never with `prompt=create` or `qauth_link`, and only while the interaction UI and passkey sign-in are on (else `invalid_request`).

post.description: Submit the consent decision. CSRF-protected; re-uses the authorize params to issue a code on Allow.

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 9449 §10: the base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the DPoP key to bind the authorization code to. Read only when the server has DPoP on.

get.description: Renders the session-cookie login page. `return_to` is a relative path to redirect to after a successful sign-in. Issue #150.

post.description: Submit the session-cookie login form. Sets __Host-qauth_session on success.

get.description: The "sign in with a passkey" page (#651): runs the browser's passkey ceremony for the interaction's `webauthn_get` step, current or offered beside the password, and posts the result to the answer endpoint. Its options name no account. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The "add a passkey" page (#651): runs the browser's registration ceremony for the interaction's `webauthn_create` step, offered after a sign-in, and posts the result to the answer endpoint, or declines the offer. At a registration it creates the account by passkey alone, with a link to the address step; after a recovery code it adds the new passkey in place of a lost one (#655). Needs the flow cookie; refused from another site. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The "save your recovery codes" page (#649): the new set of recovery codes of the interaction's `recovery_codes` step, shown once, and the confirmation the step needs. Needs the flow cookie; refused from another site. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The "use a recovery code" page (#649): the form of the interaction's `recovery_code` step, current or offered beside another step (the sign-in's first offer, for the lost passkey of an account with no address, #655), with the error of a refused code. `Cache-Control: no-store`.
Resume a pending authorization request after login. The handle is single-use and resolves ONLY to an authorize URL this server minted. Issue #316.

The "enter the code from your authenticator app" page (#653): the form of the interaction's `totp` step, with the error of a refused code and, when the step offers it, a recovery code in its place. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The "set up an authenticator app" page (#653): the new secret of the interaction's `totp_setup` step as a QR code and as text, and the form of its first code, which binds the secret. Needs the flow cookie; refused from another site. `Cache-Control: no-store`.
A provider button of the sign-in page (#639): back to the page's authorization request, routed to the upstream provider `type` with `qauth_upstream`.
Start the upstream provider `type` an authorization request routes to (#639), in the interaction the authorization endpoint started: the waiting page sends the browser to the provider.

The `upstream_link` step's page (#670): an upstream provider proved an identity no account holds; "I already have an account", which goes on to the sign-in to that account, or a new account when the realm allows one. The form posts to the Interaction API's answer endpoint. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The page of an upstream link the finish refused (#670): the identity is already linked to another account, the account already has one of the provider, or the account cannot be linked. Nothing was changed, and nothing goes to the client. No flow sends the browser here any more: a refused link comes back to the ceremony page as the `upstream_link` step with its reason (#1081). It stays until the cut-over (#709). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.description: Submit the form of the emailed verification link (GET /auth/verify): the token and the account password. Verifies as POST /auth/verify does and answers a page with the status that route answers.

get.description: Renders the wallet-linking confirmation screen for the signed-in user. Issue #238.

post.description: Starts a wallet-linking flow for the signed-in user and issues an OID4VP presentation request for a wallet on this device. Linking is same-device only (ADR-013, amended 2026-11-07): the form field `device` accepts only `this`, which is also what an absent field means, and `other` (cross-device) is refused with `400` `validation_error`. Issues #238, #405.

get.description: Re-renders a wallet-linking flow in progress, completing it if the wallet has responded. Also the no-JavaScript refresh path. Issue #238.
Renders the wallet sign-in screen, which collects the account identifier the user asserts (ADR-009). Issue #239.

post.description: Starts a wallet sign-in: records the asserted account identifier and issues an OID4VP presentation request. Issue #239.

get.description: Re-renders a wallet sign-in in progress, advancing it if the wallet has responded. Also the no-JavaScript refresh path. Issue #239.
Polled by the wallet sign-in screen. Reports whether the direct_post presentation response has arrived, and completes the sign-in when it has. Issue #239.

Same-device return leg of a wallet sign-in (OID4VP 1.0 §8.2 / §14.2, HAIP 1.0 §5.1). The wallet redirects the browser here with the single-use Response Code (43 base64url characters) it received from the direct_post Response Endpoint; the code is spent first, then matched against the flows this browser holds, and the sign-in completes only in the browser that started it. Every refusal renders one identical page. Issue #405.

tags.name: Developer API
tags.description: The developer API, `/developer/v1-rc.0`. A token reaches an operation here for its subject when its only audience is `urn:qauth:aud:developer:v1-rc.0` and it carries the developer scope of the operation's `x-qauth-class`: `qauth:developer:read` for a `read` operation, `qauth:developer:write` for a `write` one. The two are independent. A token without the scope gets 403 `forbidden` with an `insufficient_scope` challenge naming it. The operation's `x-qauth-permission` (`clients.read`, `clients.write`, ...) is a permission of that class. Only an operator can give a client the audience, and the scopes are issued only to such a client; the developer portal's token carries both.

tags.name: Account API
tags.description: The account API, `/account/v1-rc.0`. A token reaches an operation here for its subject when its only audience is `urn:qauth:aud:account:v1-rc.0` and it carries the account scope of the operation's `x-qauth-class`: `qauth:account:read` for a `read` operation, `qauth:account:write` for a `write` one. The two are independent. A token without the scope gets 403 `forbidden` with an `insufficient_scope` challenge naming it. The operation's `x-qauth-permission` (`consents.read`, `consents.write`) is a permission of that class. Only an operator can give a client the audience, and the scopes are issued only to such a client.
